title: Dynamics 365 Sales: sales skills in Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork
summary: The briefing's licensing, billing, access controls and roadmap facts are supported. Microsoft documents disagree about the user-facing Sales plugin default, which should be reported explicitly; the spending-policy and Sales access paths also need small clarifications.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature is on by default for eligible users without administrator action.
claims.quote: By default, all eligible users have access unless you configure access restrictions.
claims.fix: Keep the on field for default administrative availability, but replace 'Administrators who do nothing leave the Sales plugin on for every eligible user' with 'Administrators who do nothing leave Sales plugin access available to eligible users. Microsoft's installation page says the Cowork Sales plugin is visible but turned off by default and users can turn it on, whereas the Cowork plugin administration page says Sales integrations are enabled by default.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-sales-copilot/install-sales-app alongside the existing sources and report this explicit disagreement in Open questions rather than only asking whether the plugin is enabled.

claims.claim: Cowork access is configured through Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Identity > Select agents and services > Cowork.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration and select + Add spending policy. ... On the Scope user and group step, choose Specific groups ... On the Select agents and services step, select Cowork.
claims.fix: Use 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Identity > Scope user and group > Specific groups > group > Select agents and services > Cowork'. Identity is documented by the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits; the Cowork page supplies the user/group scope step. The omitted target-selection step is a minor, not a wrong label.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/serviceSettings adds Cowork to an existing policy using serviceId: cowork and state: enabled.
claims.quote: POST /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/serviceSettings ... Required properties are serviceId and state.

claims.claim: A service setting has no effect while the parent policy is disabled or provisioning.
claims.quote: A service setting has no effect while the parent policy is disabled or provisioning.

claims.claim: Cowork credit limits are configured through Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Identity > Select agents and services > Cowork > Set limits and alerts.
claims.quote: Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope. ... Select agents and services ... Set limits and alerts ... Select the monthly spending limit for this policy.
claims.fix: For the policy-level limit, use 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Identity > Scope user and group > Specific groups > group > Select agents and services > Cowork > Set limits and alerts > Limited monthly budget'. The Cowork migration page documents Scope user and group. The current path reaches the correct limits page but omits the target-selection step and stops before the budget control.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates credit limits through periodLimit or perUserLimit.

claims.fix: Use 'Sales > Settings > Tenant > Access settings > Allow access to Dynamics 365 Sales plugins > Dynamics 365 Sales plugins > Who can use this feature? > Set access restrictions > Allow access or Restrict access'. The missing pane heading is a minor. Allow access and Restrict access are both real list labels; 'or' indicates alternative lists, not an invented combined label. The already-cited administrator-settings-sales-app page supports Sales > Settings in the personal app.
